## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(q=n-r\), the original source presents \(J_v\) using the interval generators \(\{\bar s_\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- [source-backed] The 2024 source works integrally with \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), \(I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\); its LR argument gives \(c_{\lambda\nu}^{\rho}\ne0\Rightarrow\lambda\subseteq\rho\), with terms \(\rho\nsubseteq q^r\) zero in the quotient. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 89-94] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 136-142]
- [proved] Put \(A_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\). The actual interval ideals are
  \[
  J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda,\qquad
  J_{v^\vee}=\bigoplus_{j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu .
  \]
  Indeed, each displayed interval span contains the respective source-given generators. LR containment makes it an ideal, since every surviving product term still contains the lower rectangle. Hence it contains the generated ideal; conversely its basis elements are generators, giving equality. The quotient Schur basis makes both sums direct.
- [proved] Assume \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) is bigrassmannian: \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\). Let \(q=n-r\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and
  \[
  v^\vee:=v_{q,n-s,q-s+t,n}=v_{q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n}.
  \]
  Then \(i,j\ge1\), \(q-i=t-(r+s-n)-1\ge0\), and \(r-j=t-1\ge0\). Thus \(q\ge1\), \(1\le t^\vee=q-i+1\le q\), and
  \[
  t^\vee\le n-s\iff t\le r.
  \]
  Therefore \(1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee=q,s^\vee=n-s\le n\), and
  \[
  t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)
  =(q-i+1)-(q-s)=t>0.
  \]
  Hence \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian. Its parameters satisfy
  \[
  i^\vee=j,\quad j^\vee=i,\quad
  a^\vee=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\quad b^\vee=\min(j,i)=b.
  \]
- [proved] The integral Schur involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) is a ring involution of \(\Lambda\). Since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\), it sends \(I_{r,q}\) onto \(I_{q,r}\), inducing
  \[
  \bar\omega:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r}.
  \]
  Moreover \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'\); hence \(\bar\omega\) bijects the two displayed interval Schur bases and
  \[
  \bar\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}.
  \]
- [source-backed] Theorem 1.2 applies to every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), defines \(i,j,a,b\) as above, and states minimality of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in the integral quotient. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-78] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]
- [proved] Applying Theorem 1.2 to \(v^\vee\) gives a minimal generating family bounded above by \((j^i,b^a)\). Since
  \[
  (j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{\,j-b}),
  \]
  its pullback under \(\bar\omega^{-1}\) is
  \[
  \{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}.
  \]
  Ring isomorphisms preserve generation and minimality: a proper generating subfamily after pullback would map to a proper generating subfamily before pullback. This includes \(a=0\), with empty blocks omitted.

## Strategy
Use the original interval-generator statement, the integral quotient Schur basis, and LR truncation to prove both interval decompositions. Verify all transformed bigrassmannian inequalities, then transfer Theorem 1.2 through the integral Schur involution.
